9
A ball of mass 2.0 kg travels horizontally with a speed of 4.0 m s–1. The ball collides with a wall
and rebounds in the opposite direction with a speed of 2.8 m s–1. The time of the collision is
150 ms.
What is the average force exerted on the wall?
A
16 N
B
37 N
C
53 N
D
91 N

hints: Notice the ball rebounds in the opposite direction, so take one direction as positive and give the $2.8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ velocity the opposite sign to the $4.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ velocity.
Recall impulse equals change in momentum, $F\Delta t = m(v-u)$, so the $150 \text{ ms}$ time must be converted to $0.15 \text{ s}$ before dividing.
Remember the calculated force is the force on the ball, then use Newton's third law to state the equal magnitude force exerted on the wall.
walkthrough: Choose a positive direction, for example towards the wall. Then $u = +4.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v = -2.8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ because the rebound is opposite.
State the impulse-momentum relation for average force on the ball: $F = m(v-u)/\Delta t$.
Calculate the velocity change: $v-u = -2.8 - 4.0 = -6.8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so the speed change is $6.8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Convert time to seconds: $\Delta t = 150 \text{ ms} = 0.15 \text{ s}$, then substitute: $F = 2.0 \times (-6.8)/0.15 \approx -91 \text{ N}$.
The negative sign means the force on the ball is away from the wall. By Newton's third law the force on the wall is equal and opposite, with magnitude about $91 \text{ N}$. This is option D

A.explanation: This uses $2.0 \times (4.0 - 2.8)/0.15 = 16 \text{ N}$, which subtracts the speeds and ignores that rebound reverses velocity direction.

B.explanation: This uses only the rebound momentum $2.0 \times 2.8/0.15 \approx 37 \text{ N}$, which ignores the initial $4.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ momentum that must also be reversed.

C.explanation: This uses only the incident momentum $2.0 \times 4.0/0.15 \approx 53 \text{ N}$, which ignores the additional change needed to send the ball back at $2.8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: The total velocity change is $4.0 + 2.8 = 6.8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, giving $F = 2.0 \times 6.8/0.15 \approx 91 \text{ N}$ on the ball and, by Newton's third law, $91 \text{ N}$ on the wall.
